Hi Vanessa,

Hope you had a good weekend. We're finalizing our vendor SOC 2 and connectivity reviews for a pilot that must keep EU customer traffic inside EU zones and use private peering where possible. Security asked for: 
- A brief attestation that Redwood can host and serve the workload from EU-only regions (including which AZs/regions are used).
- The technical runbook for VPC peering / private link setup (step-by-step) and any required ASN/IP ranges.
- A fallback connectivity plan in case Private Link/Peering isn't available (e.g., site-to-site VPN, forced egress controls).
- Confirmation about KMS separation (customer-managed keys or partitioned tenant keys) and audit log retention (where logs live and retention windows).

Can you send a consolidated package we can drop into our SIG/CAIQ responses? Ideally we need something we can hand to our InfoSec by 2026-12-27.

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide a single ZIP-style evidence pack and a short attestation letter. High-level answers: 
- Yes: Redwood supports hosting and serving from EU-only regions (we currently run in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 for the hosted and private offerings; Dedicated pools can be pinned to those AZs).
- We have a documented VPC peering/private link runbook. I’m attaching a version we use for enterprise onboarding and a CSV of IP ranges you can whitelist.
- Fallback: we recommend a site-to-site IPsec VPN with explicit routing + egress enforcement; we include a short runbook for failover and a recommended health-check cadence.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys via KMS in EU regions and also logical key partitioning in our platform; audit logs are retained in EU region by default for Private deployments (90 days standard, extended retention options available).

I’ve looped in Karthik for the technical specifics and Mina for the compliance artifacts (SOC 2 cert). We’ll try to get your full pack over by Tue/27 unless you need it sooner.

Alex — following Vanessa's note, adding the technical checklist you can paste into your SIG response: 

1) Regions & isolation
- Supported EU regions: eu-west-1 (Ireland) and eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). For Private deployments we offer single-region pinning per customer project.
- Tenant isolation: logical tenant segmentation enforced at the runtime and network layer; Dedicated pools per tenant are available for strict isolation.

2) Peering / Private Link (preferred)
- Steps (high level):
  a) Exchange account IDs and VPC IDs
  b) Create peering request from Crestline VPC -> Redwood VPC (we provide peering acceptance role)
  c) Configure route tables to send app subnets to peering attachment
  d) Apply security group rules (we provide suggested rules in the runbook)
  e) Verify with connectivity tests (we include curl + mTLS test commands)
- Required network details: see ip_ranges_2026-12.csv (includes service endpoints and egress IPs for EU regions).

3) Fallback: IPsec site-to-site VPN
- When peering isn’t possible, configure an IPsec tunnel with the following:
  - Primary: AES-256 / SHA-2; IKEv2 preferred
  - BGP optional (we recommend static routes for simpler auditability)
  - BFD for faster failover where supported
- Failover plan: healthcheck every 30s, automatic routing failover to tunnel within 60s; we provide scripts to monitor and alert.

4) KMS & keys
- Customer-managed keys: supported via EU KMS (bring-your-own-key) and configured per-deployment.
- Logical key partitioning: we use tenant-scoped CMK wrapping for hosted Private deployments where BYOK isn't enabled.

5) Logging & retention
- Audit logs (access and admin) are stored in EU logging buckets for EU-hosted/private deployments by default.
- Default retention: 90 days; extended retention (365/730) can be configured as an add-on.

6) Test/validation artifacts included
- mTLS handshake test steps, sample traceroutes, and curl probes.

If your InfoSec would like we can produce a one-page attestation letter signed by our Head of Compliance.

—Karthik
